outline.title: 停电后的天文馆 / The Planetarium After the Storm
outline.summary: 暴雨让社区天文馆的控制系统停止工作。Noah、Ms. Rivera、Mina和管理员Dr. Hall没有冒险强行启动设备，而是根据记录、实时读数、已经完成的修复和安全要求逐步排查。团队为传感器测试准备了现实方案和备用方案，最终安全打开穹顶并按时举行活动。

chapters.title: 控制室上锁 / The Locked Control Room
chapters.summary: Noah和Ms. Rivera来到社区天文馆准备晚上的开放活动，却发现控制室被锁住，主电源也在暴雨后停止工作。Noah在旧值班记录中找到备用钥匙的位置，Ms. Rivera联系管理员Dr. Hall确认安全流程，两人进入控制室并发现一只被水浸湿的保险盒。
chapters.knowledgePointRecommendationSummary: Use Past simple to narrate the completed discovery and entry into the control room.

chapters.title: 控制台上的信号 / Signals on the Console
chapters.summary: 控制台重新通电后，指示灯不断闪烁，穹顶却仍然不动。Noah观察此刻正在变化的电压读数，Ms. Rivera对照设备平时的运行规则，发现冷却风扇现在没有转动。两人决定先处理风扇，而不是强行启动穹顶。
chapters.knowledgePointRecommendationSummary: Contrast actions happening now with the console's normal operating behaviour.

chapters.title: 已经完成的修复 / What the Team Has Repaired
chapters.summary: 同学Mina带来干燥工具，三人清理保险盒并重新连接风扇。Noah逐项汇报团队已经完成的修复和仍未解决的问题；Ms. Rivera根据这些最新结果判断主系统可以进入低功率测试，但穹顶传感器仍需要检查。
chapters.knowledgePointRecommendationSummary: Use Present perfect for completed repairs whose results matter to the current test.

chapters.title: 安全测试 / The Safety Test
chapters.summary: Dr. Hall远程说明安全要求：测试前必须清空穹顶轨道，所有人必须站在黄色线外，Noah还需要确认紧急停止按钮。团队逐项完成要求，随后发现一把维修梯仍挡在轨道旁，于是暂停测试并把它移走。
chapters.knowledgePointRecommendationSummary: Use have to and must for external safety requirements and strong necessary actions.

chapters.title: 如果穹顶打开 / If the Dome Opens
chapters.summary: 正式测试前，Noah比较现实方案和假设方案：如果传感器通过，他们就按原计划开放天文馆；如果传感器仍然失败，他们会把活动改成小型星图课。传感器最终通过，穹顶顺利打开，团队保留星图课作为备用方案并按时迎接参观者。
chapters.knowledgePointRecommendationSummary: Use real and hypothetical if-clauses to compare the available plans without changing the confirmed outcome.

args.title: 控制室上锁 / The Locked Control Room
args.cleanText: After the storm, Noah and Ms. Rivera arrived at the community planetarium for the evening event. They tried the locked control-room door and noticed that the main power was off. While Ms. Rivera called Dr. Hall, Noah checked the old duty records. He soon found a note about a spare key. Dr. Hall confirmed the safety process by phone before they entered. Noah collected the spare key from a labeled drawer, and Ms. Rivera opened the door carefully. Inside, they saw water near the equipment. Noah discovered a wet fuse box beside the silent console, so they stopped and recorded the damage before touching anything.

args.title: 控制台上的信号 / Signals on the Console
args.cleanText: After the fuse box was dried, power returned to the console, but the dome remained still. Several lights flashed. Noah watched the voltage display and said, “The reading is changing every few seconds.” Ms. Rivera replied, “The system usually shows a steady number.” They were recording the changing figures in the repair log. Noah then noticed another difference. “The cooling fan normally runs whenever the console is on, but it is not moving now,” he said. Ms. Rivera asked him to check the fan connection instead of forcing the dome motor. They chose this safer approach, marked the fan as the next priority, and were monitoring the flashing signals.

args.title: 已经完成的修复 / What the Team Has Repaired
args.cleanText: Mina arrived with dry cloths and safe cleaning tools. Together, the students cleaned the fuse box and reconnected the cooling fan while Ms. Rivera checked each step. Before the low-power test, Noah reported, “We have dried the wet area, and Mina has secured the loose cable. The fan has started again.” He continued, “We have recorded every repair in the log, but we have not tested the dome sensor yet.” Ms. Rivera studied the latest results and said the completed work had made a low-power test possible. The team have restarted the main system successfully, but the sensor warning remained. They have marked that final issue as unresolved and prepared a separate inspection.

args.title: 安全测试 / The Safety Test
args.cleanText: Dr. Hall joined by video and explained the safety requirements. “The dome track has to be completely clear before any test. Everyone must stand behind the yellow line, and Noah has to confirm the emergency stop button,” he said. The team began to check each requirement on a written checklist. Mina inspected the track and found a maintenance ladder beside it. “We must move this first,” Noah said. They paused the test, had to move the heavy ladder together, and checked the whole track again. Noah then had to test the emergency button without starting the motor. Only after every safety condition was satisfied did Ms. Rivera request Dr. Hall’s approval.

args.title: 如果穹顶打开 / If the Dome Opens
args.cleanText: Before the final sensor test, Noah compared both plans. “If the sensor passes, we will open the planetarium as planned,” he said. “If it fails again, we will hold a small star-map lesson instead.” Mina prepared the lesson materials so the team would have a practical alternative without ignoring safety. Noah also considered a less likely situation: “If the dome stopped during the event, we would close the room calmly.” Then they began the sensor test. It passed, and the dome opened safely. “If visitors arrive on time, we can welcome them as planned,” Ms. Rivera said. They kept the star-map lesson as a backup and greeted the first visitors on schedule.
